sentences.text: Appearance:
Shri Abhishek Gilke - Advocate for the appellants.
Shri Manoj Jain, learned counsel for the respondent   ORDER 01.
With consent of learned counsel for the parties the matter is finally heard.

02. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants / claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 31.8.2023 passed in MACC No.103/2021 by the IIIrd Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Shajapur whereby a total sum of Rs.11,03,800/- has been awarded to the appellants / claimants by way of compensation.

03. Short facts of the case are that on 18.10.2020 at 1.00 PM deceased along with Kamal Malviya was going from Shajapur to his village Samgimana by his motorcycle bearing registration No. M.P.
70 MV 0504.

When they reached near Karedi Naka on Shajapur Dupada Road at that time respondent No.2 driver of offending Pickup Van bearing registration No. NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29241 2 MA-6744-2023 M.P. 14 GC 0396 driven the said Van rashly and negligently and dashed the motorcycle of the deceased resulting into death of the deceased due to the mishap.
04. Thereafter the appellants filed an application under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, 1988 for award of compensation to them on account of his death.

The application was contested by respondent /
Insurance Co. by filing its written statement to the same.

Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the claims tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.11,03,800/- for the loss on death of Vishal Malviya (deceased).

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the tribunal has incorrectly assessed the income of the deceased.
The deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by doing the work as a mason.
However, the claims tribunal has assessed his income on notional basis by treating him an unskilled labourer at Rs.6500/- per month.
He submits that even this assessment is not correct in view of the fact that infact, the minimum wages at the relevant time was Rs.8,400/-.
The tribunal has erred in treating the minimum wages at Rs.6500/- as it has taken only one part of the wages as prescribed by the competent authority ie., minimum basic pay.
However the dearness allowance has been excluded.
He thus prays for enhancement of compensation.

06. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.1 / Insurance Co. refers to the findings recorded by the claims tribunal in para 36 as well as the statement of AW.1 and points out that the claimants /
appellants were not able to prove that the deceased was working as mason.
As such the tribunal NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29241 3 MA-6744-2023 has correctly treated him as an unskilled labourer and has assessed his income at Rs.6,500/- per month.
He thus prays for dismissal of the appeal.

07. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
08.

On perusal of the findings recorded by the claims tribunal as well as the statement of Sundarbai AW.1, it is seen that there was no material at all to establish that the deceased was working as mason and earning Rs.15000/- per month.
As such the tribunal has correctly treated the deceased as an unskilled labourer.
However, from the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority, it is seen that the wages were Rs.8400/- per month.
The tribunal while considering the minimum wages has completely overlooked the component of dearness allowance while taking the income.

As such the income of the deceased is taken as per the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority at Rs.8,400/- per month and, therefore, the compensation for loss of dependency would now changed to Rs.12,70,080/-.

After deducting the already awarded amount of Rs.9,82,800/- (amount towards dependency), the appellant is now entitled for Rs.2,87,280/- over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition before the claims tribunal.
09. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed and disposed off.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
